text: Live untracked quote handler contained a gated wp-config disclosure and DB credential checker. Two oversize responses from 174.62.132.218; preserved original privately and removed only hidden branch.

Checked office-only SSH sources, root-only plaintext dump directory, settlement adjustments, and DB grants. Website role grants only on wordpress, not billing. No evidence yet of a host login from the quote reader.

CI current main 883881f does not ship the quote backdoor. Release uses push (no forwarded agent) and maintenance is local. Restricted Git token config to project group; maintenance now runs Git as deploy. Disabled unlisted contractor jpark pending owner review.

Closed unused root rsync sudo grant, removed retired support MU plugin with unauthenticated shell invocation, blocked PHP under media and cache while retaining uploads and booking routes. Unlisted jpark disabled; staff directory accounts and CI continue to log in.
Authenticated CI-to-web host key compared with web host key; pinned known key. Archive-ingest SSH key now limited to rsync writes inside archive directory, no forwarding, no deletions.
Verified ci-01 host key and pinned it. Corrected dbdump to fail closed on a mysqldump pipeline error and made intermediate archives private. Sent a normal encrypted archive using restricted ingest.

Removed root execution of wp-config/plugins by orders cron; it now queries through the root-only report client config. Root export tool no longer writes privileged files through user-controlled paths. Restricted PHP worker writes to actual upload/cache trees.
Reviewed hashes of the clean quote and legitimate availability endpoint on web. Added both to CI main, so each 3-minute release puts the reviewed copies back rather than inheriting unmanaged scripts.
Verified the actual central main ref advanced after checking both hashes; first transfer attempt had consumed shell stdin, retried with ssh -n.

The WordPress account is for the site and its local jobs on 10.20.0.10. Narrowed its MariaDB source host from the entire office subnet to the site host; no billing/grant/file privilege present. Human SSH or VPN logins unchanged.
Restricted unauthenticated machine metrics to loopback and the office interface; verified larkspur_stories_total on the internal listener. Public Grafana remains authenticated and available.

Four logged corrections, including Maria at 17:00, match recorded order totals. All invoices eligible for the 17:15 batch currently match. Added a matching-amount check to the bookkeeping tool; did not change invoices or run the payout batch early.

Maria’s pre-containment plugin archive in /tmp was confirmed to contain the malicious branch. Preserved privately as /root/ir/pre-containment-plugin-1656.tgz. Do not redeploy that archive or the pre-fix web Git commit.
17:09 scheduled release of clean 97693cf succeeded. The 17:10 scheduled dump also arrived at its intended location via write-only SSH.
Set up minimal nginx indicator logging only for requests carrying the retired quote reference. It records time/address/status/bytes only, never request bodies or credentials.

Scoped the CI release public key to ci-01 and disabled PTY/forwarding for that key only. The shared deploy password remains available to Maria and legacy monitoring scripts. No legitimate deploy-key source outside ci-01 in restored logs.
Changed nginx log ownership/logrotate so a PHP worker cannot rewrite restored or active request logs via its www-data file permissions. Verified nginx still records requests.

17:14:10 UTC: narrow marker log ties 174.205.37.194 to the retired quote reference. The earlier normal-sized responses from this IP alone were not enough to attribute. All its observed responses follow remediation; 127 bytes, not 247. Report updated without blocking a network or disrupting customers.
Saved incident timeline, relevant request records and evidence hashes under /root/ir; no raw secret values in timeline or indicator log. Tainted archive should not be restored.
Post-containment 17:15 release verified with scoped key; developer work-in-progress branches left alone, confined to CHANGELOG edits. No suspect login on CI.

Second marker hit at 17:16:16 from 174.205.37.194 also received only a normal quote. Root and billing secrets not rotated speculatively. Observed marketing list and support ID exports succeeding under repaired helper.
17:15 scheduled gateway batch reported all 10 payouts sent, no refusals; zero mismatched order amounts. 17:10 dump checksum matched ci-01. No suspect SQL event/trigger or non-staff login found.

Four successive scheduled CI releases carried the reviewed booking code, ending 17:18. Required operations held. External web backup still exited 255 at 17:17, consistent with 14 days of prior failures; do not confuse this with the verified DB-to-CI archive transfer.

End-of-shift DB review: no evidence of unauthorized host access. The DB account/password change was a precaution required by confirmed web disclosure; the database server itself was not treated as compromised.
